key_insight: By using topological conjugacy to transform free-boundary PDEs into equivalent fixed-domain problems, neural operators can be trained reliably on the transformed space and then mapped back to recover accurate solutions on moving domains.
problem_solved: Standard neural operators assume fixed spatial domains and struggle with PDEs whose boundaries evolve over time (free-boundary problems such as glacier melt), making it hard to learn and predict boundary motion and coupled fields.
method: Define a topological-conjugacy mapping that converts the original free-boundary problem into an equivalent PDE on a fixed reference domain.
Train a neural operator in the transformed (fixed-domain) coordinate system to learn the solution operator across instances efficiently.
Apply the inverse conjugacy map to reconstruct solutions and boundary evolution on the original moving domain, preserving physical consistency.
impact: This framework extends neural operators to a broad class of realistic, time-evolving physical systems (e.g., geophysical and engineering problems) without redesigning core architectures, making operator learning applicable to moving-boundary scenarios with improved accuracy and generalization.
